note: Every number here traces to PATEL-HANDOFF.md §6/§9, itself sourced from the client's Patel_Retail_data_Munshot.xlsx and Peer_Model.xlsx. Nothing in this file was estimated or invented — derived figures (store EBITDA) are computed at runtime in public/js/economics.js from the reported inputs below, not hardcoded, so the arithmetic stays visible.

unit_economics.sqft_per_store_note: The same 5,000 sq ft blended average applied to all 53 stores uniformly — not a per-store measurement (per-store sq ft was not supplied and isn't coming). Anything derived from this figure inherits the estimate label.
unit_economics.gross_margin_pct_note: Store file states this as a range ("16-17%", cell L18) — 16.5% is the range midpoint, used for every gross-margin calculation in this dashboard.
unit_economics.private_label_pct_note: Store file gives this as a single exact figure (cell L19: 0.175), not a range — no midpoint involved.
unit_economics.source: client file Patel_Retail_data_Munshot.xlsx (Aug 2026), verified cell-by-cell against the primary source

revenue_mix.non_food_note: Store file states this as a range ("20-21%", cell L14) — 20.5% is the range midpoint.
revenue_mix.merchandise_note: Store file states this as a range ("9-10%", cell L15) — 9.5% is the range midpoint.

own_brand.note: ₹2.2cr on ~₹449cr retail revenue (~0.5%) — small, but ₹1cr of it sells outside Patel's own stores, which reads as brand behaviour rather than shelf-filling.

private_label_pct.note: Patel's private label is ~2x DMart's, but far below Vishal/Trent — 'very high own-brand' doesn't survive peer context.

revenue_per_sqft_year.resolution_note: The two client files disagree by ~28% on this single most important unit-economics figure. This dashboard uses the store-file value (₹17,280) for every calculation — the peer-model figure is shown for reference only, never averaged in and never picked silently.

peer_model_bugs.note: All 10 documented in PATEL-HANDOFF.md §10, from the client's Peer_Model.xlsx. Status is honest per bug: 'fixed' means this dashboard shows the corrected figure below; 'not_applicable' means the bug doesn't carry over because this dashboard doesn't build that metric at all; 'needs_source_file' means the correct value was never given anywhere in the handoff — only that the current one is wrong — and re-opening the original spreadsheet is the only way to fix it.

store_pnl_reconciliation.flag_note: Building EBITDA from the client's own per-store unit economics gives ~5.4% of sales, before any head-office cost. The peer model claims 7.9% EBITDA at the company level for the same B2C business — a company-level margin should come in lower than store-level once overhead is added, not higher. Two plausible causes: the peer model's B2C/export revenue split may be misallocating margin, or the store-level inputs are conservative. Left open for the client to clarify, not resolved here.
store_pnl_reconciliation.total_company_note: Not a B2C-specific quirk — the peer model derives Patel's entire B2C column by applying one fixed 45% share to total-company revenue, EBITDA and PAT, and that same factor cancels out of the margin ratio. So the 7.9% figure is identical whether read at the B2C or total-company level; the contradiction holds either way.
store_pnl_reconciliation.note: store_ebitda_l / store_ebitda_pct are computed at runtime from the reported inputs above (see public/js/economics.js) rather than stored pre-computed, so the arithmetic stays auditable on screen.
